newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Vitoria says July cargo traffic up 30.2pct.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Vitoria says July cargo traffic up 30.2pct.

text.p: Cargo traffic at Vitoria airport in northern Spain rose 30.2 percent in July, compared with the same month last year, to 2,847 tonnes, the airport authority said.
This follows a 35.3 percent increase in June and takes the total so far this year to 16,141 tonnes, a 23.3 percent increase on 1996.
International non-European Union (EU) freight accounted for 1,244 tonnes of the July total, EU freight for 908 tonnes and domestic cargo only 696 tonnes.

Vitoria, which started commercial cargo operations in 1994, has become an important transit point for fresh fruit, frozen fish and mail. The latter accounts for an increasingly large proportion of the airport's business as DHL Worldwide Express expands its Vitoria hub.

Some 46 percent of the airport's cargo business was mail in the first four months of this year, figures from the local Chamber of Commerce show. This was up from 33 percent for 1996 as a whole. Perishable goods made up 42 percent of cargo in the January to end April period, down from 53 percent last year, and general cargo accounted for 12 percent from 14 percent in 1996.
